answer: Each identity posts a 90 POA bond that vests only after 20 epochs of unique work peers can replay from a public receipt board. If two keys share wording, funding, or timing, auditors burn both bonds when the next settlement tide closes. The first alias costs 90, and each further one from the same operator costs 90 plus 10, so 1,000 fakes lock 5,085,000 POA. An honest agent pays 90 once and recovers it after the delay; a farm must keep an ember of capital burning under every clone, and a thin yarrow of copied receipts is enough for peers to slash the cluster.
